title: Legal Methodology Layer
description: Schema for the layer that sits between raw legal-text entity extraction (e.g. Isaacus/Kanon NER) and an LLM. It encodes doctrinal structure -- what a competent lawyer knows before reading a single clause -- so the LLM receives structured grounding instead of just spans of text with entity tags.

Authority.description: A single source of law: a statute, a case, a restatement section, a treatise passage. Weight is NOT stored as a hand-picked number -- it is computed at query time by methodology_layer.weighting from (type, court_level, whether it is binding in the jurisdiction being queried). See weighting.py for the formula.

home_jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction that produced this authority, e.g. US-CA, US-NY, US-federal-9th-cir, US-model (for UCC/Restatement, which are model law, binding nowhere on their own).

binding_in.description: Jurisdictions in which this authority is binding (not merely persuasive). A model-law or out-of-jurisdiction case is persuasive everywhere it is not listed here.

source_case.description: Authority id of the citing case

target_case.description: Authority id of the cited case

on_issue.description: The specific doctrinal point the relation concerns, not just 'the case in general'.

source_bound_by_target.description: True when source_case is under a vertical stare decisis obligation to follow target_case (e.g. a federal circuit applying state law is bound by that state's highest court) regardless of whether it agrees. This is the field that lets 'criticizes' and 'follows' coexist truthfully.

DoctrinalRule.description: An interpretive principle / canon of construction, expressed as a machine-checkable trigger plus the authority that grounds it.

jurisdiction_scope.description: Jurisdictions where this rule is treated as binding; empty/absent means 'general common-law canon, weight depends on local adoption'.

trigger.description: Structural precondition on the fact pattern that must hold for this rule to be considered at all.

params.description: Rule-type-specific trigger parameters (e.g. {source: course_of_performance} or {pattern: specific_list_then_general_catchall}); intentionally left open-ended since its shape varies per trigger type.

priority.description: Lower number = consulted earlier in the doctrinal hierarchy. Used to order applicable_rules in an InterpretiveAnnotation, not to hide a fixed answer.

supersedes.description: Rule ids this rule takes priority over when both are triggered and conflict.

DoctrinalHierarchy.description: A named, ordered ladder of DoctrinalRules for a sub-area of law, e.g. the UCC 1-303 order of resort for interpreting agreements.

ordered_rule_ids.description: Rule ids in the order they are to be consulted; earlier entries control over later ones when they conflict.

InterpretiveAnnotation.description: The unit actually handed to the LLM in place of (or alongside) raw entity spans: a structured interpretive brief for one clause in one jurisdiction under one fact pattern.

threshold_determination.description: The gating question: is extrinsic/contextual evidence even admissible here, and under what test.

conflicting_authority.description: PrecedentRelation ids surfacing tension the LLM should be aware of (e.g. a binding case that a later court criticized but could not depart from).

recommended_interpretive_posture.description: A structural summary, not a legal conclusion: what doctrinal path applies and why, in one or two sentences.
